doc.title: Larry Gold interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2025

title: Hearing your first charts played and the Synclavier
summary: The cringe moment of hearing a score played; Gold uses a Synclavier to sketch arrangements.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I thought of a comment. Recently I interviewed Alan Broadbent and I asked him what it was like the very first time you write something and you hear it played. And he described it as a "cringe moment." Because you never quite now how it's going to lay until they really start to play it.

Well especially in the '70s and the '80s before we had all these computers. Now I can do a little dubbing, I have a Synclavier so I can put the song in my Synclavier and do a little sketch and I can listen to it. It's not the same at all but at least I can hear — I can play with the voicing. I can play with a lot of different things. You know I start editing out things more than I do adding.
I saw a video just earlier today of you and I said, "What is that keyboard in the background?" And that's probably what it was.
Yeah. It's got a lot of dials and buttons.
